sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 3.3% a year from $65.1 billion in FY2017 to $87.0 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F201].

FY2019 was the break: operating income fell 58.9% [D97] on an $8.3 billion asset impairment charge [X112], which the FY2020 filing attributes to currency devaluations, decelerating grooming category growth and tougher competition in Shave Care [P62].
FY2020 reversed it, with operating income up 186.2% [D148] as $8.3 billion of the increase came from the base-period Shave Care charge [P71].
Since then the trend is slow and steady: revenue grew 2.0% a year over FY2023 to FY2026 [D664], and operating margin of 22.7% in FY2026 sits 0.6pp above the 22.1% window median [F30][D648].
The US was the growth engine for most of the window, contributing +3.7pp of FY2022 revenue growth [D524] and still +1.3pp in FY2025 [D533], before fading to +0.1pp in FY2026 [D536].
In FY2026 the Non-US business carried growth instead, contributing +3.1pp [D511] as net sales rose 3% on favorable foreign exchange of 2% and pricing of 1% [P26].
Fabric & Home Care is the largest segment at 34.8% of revenue and added +0.8pp in FY2026 [D541][D543], while Beauty added +1.3pp on 7.1% growth [D603][D602].
Operating costs grew 2.1pp faster than revenue in FY2026 [D482], and operating income fell 3.4% against revenue growth of 3.3% [D458][D457].
Diluted EPS rose 1.7% [D461] against net income growth of 0.5% [D459], helped by a 1.3% reduction in the diluted share count [D476].
Operating margin of 22.7% in FY2026 [F30] is above the 22.1% window median but below the 24.3% FY2025 high [D648][D647], and well above the 8.1% FY2019 low [D646].

The 1.6pp operating-margin decline in FY2026 [D470] came mostly from cost of revenue, a -1.0pp effect [D483], as gross margin fell on unfavorable category mix partly offset by lower commodity costs and productivity savings [P5].
SG&A added a further -0.6pp [D485] on higher marketing spending, partly offset by lower overhead [P5].
In FY2026 net margin of 18.4% sat 4.3pp below the 22.7% operating margin [F50][F30], as other non-operating income of $1.1 billion [X108] and a 20.8% tax rate [D443] partly offset the gap.
Operating cash flow of $19.6 billion was 1.22x net income in FY2026 [F80][F40][D444], above the 0.87x peer median for free cash flow to net income [D679].
The 9.8% operating cash flow increase [D462] came as net earnings plus non-cash items generated about $19.5 billion, with working capital adding $29 million [P3].
Free cash flow of $15.1 billion was a 17.4% margin [F100][D441], above the 17.2% window median [D654], after capex of $4.4 billion, or 5.1% of revenue [F90][D440].
Capex ran at 1.40x D&A [D446], the highest ratio in the window, as capital spending grew 16.9% [D464].
The company carries net debt of $24.2 billion, net cash of -27.8% of revenue [D450][D451], against a -1.0% peer median and a 33rd percentile among six staples peers [D677][D676].
Long-term debt fell 8.6% to $22.8 billion in FY2026 [F190][D468], while cash rose 4.0% to $9.9 billion [F140][D466].
Buybacks of $5.0 billion plus dividends of $10.2 billion [X134][X144] equaled 100.7% of free cash flow [D453], and the diluted share count fell 1.3% [D476].
The payout is funded at the edge of free cash flow, so the balance sheet has little room to absorb a weak cash year without more borrowing.
The current ratio was 0.68x in FY2026 [F180], below 1.0x and below the 0.72x window median [D663], a condition flagged as high severity [R1].
A sub-1.0x current ratio is normal for this business model given its negative working capital, so the flag is largely structural rather than a liquidity warning.
Buybacks and dividends exceeded free cash flow in FY2025 at 116.6% and FY2026 at 100.7% [D402][D453], the medium-severity flag [R2].
Two years of payouts above free cash flow mean capital return depends on continued operating cash generation, and any conversion slip would force a choice between buybacks and debt.
Watch operating margin in the FY2027 10-K: a print below the 22.1% window median [D648] would confirm the FY2026 cost pressure, while a recovery above 22.7% [F30] would reverse it.
Watch capex as a share of revenue in the FY2027 10-K: a rise above the FY2026 5.1% [D440] would extend the capital-intensity trend.
Watch buybacks plus dividends as a share of free cash flow in the FY2027 10-K: a reading above the FY2026 100.7% [D453] would keep the payout above cash generation.
